title: W-3b: refuse or flag request-rewriting override headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-Original-URL, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-Host); needs opum-doc design
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-3 (second half), sec-b F2. The Host and framing names of W-3 are delivered by WCLI-84 (opum-ai/ward-cli#208, DEC-248); no duplicate is filed. DEC-248 does not rule on the override headers, which several frameworks honour, so an approved method GET can execute as DELETE. Design question for opum-doc: refuse, or flag prominently in the approval prompt, which names, and the snapshot-version consequence. Not buildable until a design is recorded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: opum-doc records a design for override headers: refuse or flag, the exact name set, and the version policy
The recorded design is implemented with tests in both directions, and profileSnapshotVersion follows ADR 0018

implementationNotes: DESIGN RULING, opum-doc, 2026-10-30T15:57:41Z, recorded on ODOC-552, relayed by team-lead. Verbatim: "REFUSE them; do not flag. Use the same reserved-name mechanism as W-3/WCLI-84: case-insensitive, at profile validation. The refused set: X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method, X-Method-Override, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded. Reason: each one lets the request differ from what the approval prompt showed (method, path or authority), and a prompt flag is the layout surface W-5 already shows can be spoofed. An existing profile that declares one is refused on load with an error naming the header, under the snapshot-version policy, never silently stripped. If a real API needs one later, that is a new design ask, not an exception in code." The first acceptance criterion (opum-doc records a design) is met by this ruling; the build is briefed separately after its floor check.

Opus review of ward-cli#208 (verbatim): "landing WCLI-98 separately means profileSnapshotVersion 4 and a second fleet re-approval; its refused set must also apply to auth.name, not only to ordinary headers, since both now share isRefusedHeaderName (profile.ts:232-235)."

opum-doc ruling, 2026-10-30T16:29:41Z (to be recorded on ODOC-552), verbatim: "FOLD WCLI-98 into WCLI-84's snapshot version. One profile re-approval for the operator, not two.
- No Ward release (no tag, no main promotion) is cut until WCLI-98 has landed on dev alongside #208. Both changes ride one profileSnapshotVersion. If #208 has already bumped it to 3, WCLI-98 stays at 3 rather than going to 4, which is safe because nothing at 3 has been released or approved anywhere.
- Yes, the refused set covers auth.name through the shared isRefusedHeaderName: a secret header may not be named any of the nine override headers, Host, or the framing and hop-by-hop names. Prove it both ways in WCLI-98's tests.
- Plan the operator's single sitting to cover everything that forces a re-approval: these snapshot changes and the W-1 rebuild, whose new cdhash needs the keychain approved again (WCLI-96). Batch them into one release and one sitting, not three." This SUPERSEDES the preceding note's "profileSnapshotVersion 4 and a second fleet re-approval" observation (reviewer, ward-cli#208); both are kept so the record shows each. The refused-set-covers-auth.name half of that earlier note stands. Not built; WCLI-98 gets its own floor-checked brief after #208 lands.

Built on feat/wcli-98-refuse-override-headers per the 15:57:41Z and 16:29:41Z rulings: the nine names added to refusedHeaderNames (profile.ts), shared by ordinary headers and auth.name via isRefusedHeaderName; profileSnapshotVersion stays 3. Tests in test/header-auth.test.ts: each name as written/lower/upper in both positions, near names accepted, version asserted 3, stored v3 snapshot declaring one refused as vault_state_malformed (with positive control). Mutation control: removing x-rewrite-url turned exactly its 6 cases red. ADR 0024 amended. bun run check green (923 pass). Open design gap: the ruling says the load error names the header, but no Ward error carries a header name (WardError holds a code and an argument position only), so refusal reports profile_invalid or vault_state_malformed with no name; reported to team-lead.

opum-doc ruling A on the load-error design gap, 2026-10-30T16:35:39Z, verbatim: "A. Name the refused header using Ward's OWN canonical constant, never the profile's bytes. This is how my 15:57:41Z "error naming the header" is to be read; it was never meant to break the non-echo property.
Conditions for the commit and the review:
1. The detail is chosen by matching against the refused-name list and printing the list's entry, by index or by a constant lookup. The input string is never passed through, sliced or case-folded into the output.
2. A test declares a mixed-case spelling (for example "x-FORWARDED-host") and asserts the printed detail is byte-identical to Ward's canonical "X-Forwarded-Host".
3. A test asserts a declared header that is NOT on the list never appears in any error output, and neither does any header value.
4. The same holds at both sites, profile_invalid at declaration and vault_state_malformed at load, and for auth.name.
5. The review checks that the new detail field cannot carry anything but a member of the constant list." Built as a second commit on ward-cli#215: WardError gains refusedHeader, typed as a member of refusedHeaderCanonicalNames and filtered to the list by the constructor (condition 5); profile.ts looks the matched entry up in a folded-name to canonical Map and a proxy-* name prints the constant "Proxy-*"; vault-state.ts rethrows the load refusal as vault_state_malformed with the same detail. Mutation controls: echoing the input at the listed-name site turned conditions 2 and 4 red (22 cases); echoing at an unlisted name turned the condition-3 test red.

Correction to the earlier build note on the condition-3 mutation (review round 1, item 7). That mutation was compound: it made the unlisted-name site throw WardError with refusedHeader set to the declared name AND the constructor filter was still removed from the preceding mutation. What changed was only the detail, so the message suffix "(refused header: <name>)" printed the input; the hint and the argument position were untouched. With the constructor filter intact, the same site mutation is dropped to undefined and the test stays green, so the filter is a second line of defence the test does not distinguish from the site. The condition-3 value assertion was also vacuous (capital-S "Sentinel" against a lower-case value) and is fixed in the round-1 commit.

opum-doc ruling on finding 3, 2026-10-30T16:43:35Z, verbatim: "A, with one widening.
1. Fold "_" to "-" (after case-folding) before EVERY reserved or refused header-name lookup, not only the nine override names. That covers authorization, proxy-authorization, Host and the framing and hop-by-hop names from W-3 as well, in both positions (ordinary headers and auth.name), so Content_Length and Proxy_Authorization are caught by the same rule. My ruling's reason, that the request must not differ from what the prompt showed, is what governs here; the exact list was only the starting set.
2. Add X-Forwarded-Port, X-Forwarded-Prefix, X-Original-Host and X-Host to the refused set.
3. The printed detail stays Ward's canonical constant: X_Forwarded_Host prints "X-Forwarded-Host".
4. Tests both ways: each underscore spelling is refused at both positions, near-names stay accepted (for example X-Forwarded-Hostname, and an X-Host- prefix that is a different token), and the mutation control (dropping the fold makes exactly the underscore cases go red) is shown.
5. profileSnapshotVersion stays 3, under the fold ruling. Update the ADR to state the fold rule and the full set." Built on ward-cli#215: the fold is applied once in refusedHeaderEntry (profile.ts) and never to the output; the four names join the Map and the canonical list (26 entries). Not covered by the fold, as not ruled: the auth.name versus ordinary-header collision check still compares by case only. ADR 0024 text for this and for round 1 is blocked by the documentation lore profile budget; raised with team-lead.

opum-doc ruling, 2026-10-30T17:15:29Z, verbatim: "1. ADR 0024 budget: A. Raise the documentation profile's max_tokens to 36100, sized to your measured minimal draft. You're right that my no-raise reason was the duplicate list, and it is gone. Use one example per category; do not raise further to fit more examples. Raise the other three profiles only where lore check requires it, each to its own measured need, and state each raise and its measured count in the PR body.
2. The auth.name-versus-ordinary-header collision check: I disagree with the scope reading. Apply the same fold (case-fold, then "_" to "-") to the duplicate and collision checks too, in this PR. The fold ruling's invariant covers it: an ordinary header X_Api_Key declared next to a secret auth.name X-Api-Key reaches a CGI-style server as one variable, so one value can clobber the other, the same class as CVE-2024-45614. Adding it later would mean profileSnapshotVersion 4 and a second operator re-approval, which the fold ruling exists to avoid. Test both ways: X_Api_Key next to auth.name X-Api-Key is refused, two unrelated names are accepted, and dropping the fold from the collision check turns exactly those cases red. The ADR's (c) says the fold applies to every header-name comparison, which costs a few words.
Then round 2." Built: foldHeaderName in profile.ts is the single comparison form for the refused lookup, the duplicate check and the collision check; documentation max_tokens 36000 to 36100 (measured ~36066, no other profile needed a raise); ADR 0024 states the rule and points to refusedHeaderNames. Mutation controls: dropping the fold from the collision check turns exactly the collision test red; from the duplicate check, exactly the duplicate test red.

opum-doc ruling on ward-cli#215 ADR 0024 wording, received by the leader at 17:25:40Z (opum-doc's message carried no timestamp), verbatim: "opum-doc ruling on ward-cli#215 ADR 0024 wording: A. My 17:15:29Z "every header-name comparison" was too broad; it meant every refusal, reservation, duplicate and collision check. Narrow (c), the frontmatter summary and the profile.ts:267 comment to: "in every refused-name, reserved-name, duplicate and collision check; the approval comparison stays literal (Decision 5)". The literal approval comparison is correct: a renamed auth header must re-prompt. Add one test, if it does not already exist, proving that renaming auth.name from X-Api-Key to X_Api_Key requires a new approval. Land it with the other should-fix items in one commit, have the confirmatory review cover that commit, then land #215." Built in the round-2 should-fix commit on ward-cli#215: ADR Decision 2, the frontmatter summary and the foldHeaderName comment narrowed; two new re-approval tests in test/header-auth.test.ts (auth.name X-Api-Key to X_Api_Key reports ["auth"]; an ordinary header renamed only by underscore reports ["headers"]). Mutation controls: folding sameAuth reddened the new auth test and the existing case-only test; folding sameHeaders reddened exactly the new headers test.
